title: Marine Corps Security Force (MCSF) Guard (GySgt to Pvt) EMOS (0311, 0331, 0341, 0352, 0369, 5811), DC PP&O
raw_text:
2. MOS 8152, Marine Corps Security Force (MCSF) Guard (GySgt to Pvt) EMOS
(0311, 0331, 0341, 0352, 0369, 5811), DC PP&O

    a. Summary. The MCSF Guard will be assigned to duty with MCSF
Battalions and Fleet Antiterrorism Security Team Companies. Marines will be
in a full duty status, mentally cleared to handle weapons and ammunition, and
physically fit. They will be mentally capable of enduring the rigors of
combat, free of restrictions that hinder them from being forward deployed to
accomplish the mission. They will have the requisite knowledge to safely and
properly employ and maintain all weapons organic to the Security Force
Regiment. As a member of a quick reaction force, they will conduct offensive
infantry tactics to restore security and provide the final barrier/element of
an integrated security plan for a designated asset. Marines must also possess
skills in urban and rural land navigation and patrolling. In the grades of
Corporal through Gunnery Sergeant, as a security supervisor, the Marine will
plan, evaluate, and supervise the implementation of site specific security
plans to protect assets designated as vital to national security..

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must hold MOS 0311, 0331, 0341, 0352, 0369, or 5811.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Marine Corps Security Force Basic
Security Guard (BSG) Course (M18M4V1), Norfolk, VA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (dh), Marine Corps Security Force Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Security Guards 33-9032.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
